objective: Show captured pieces and the material count during a game (FR-20, FR-4), web only. Produce: (1) a pure function (e.g. apps/web/src/material.ts) from a FEN to, for each colour, the opponent pieces it has captured grouped by type (and ordered pawn, knight, bishop, rook, queen) and the material difference. Pieces of a colour that were captured = starting set (8P 2N 2B 2R 1Q) minus that colour's pieces on board, after first counting each piece beyond its starting count (a promotion) as a pawn still on board: e.g. White with 2 queens and 7 pawns has lost no queen and no pawn. Those captured pieces are shown on the opponent's (capturing) side. Material = sum of values on the board, pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9, king 0; so a promoted pawn counts as the new piece. (2) Next to each side's label above and below the board (add a small 'You' / 'Bot' label row if none exists; the board's top side is the bot, the bottom the player, following playerColor orientation) show that side's captured pieces, and '+N' only for the side ahead; nothing when level. Labelled so it can't be read as an engine eval (e.g. title/aria-label 'Material: +2 (piece count, not an engine evaluation)'). Use the board's input: boardFen(state) (game-state.ts:308), so takebacks, refresh rebuild and the optimistic pendingFen all just work. (3) Tests first: unit tests for the function (start position level; knight-for-pawn trade gives +2 to the knight side with the knight shown on that side; promotion to queen; underpromotion to knight; a side with two queens; takeback to an earlier FEN); a component/render test that the +N appears only on the side ahead and the labels; a Playwright E2E that makes a capture and sees the captured piece appear on the capturing side (look at the bot's typical replies in apps/web/e2e/play.spec.ts; pick a capture that's reliable, or assert generically that after any capture the counts change).
